answer: In a decentralized network, each AI agent can resemble a vine in a nebula, where nodes must connect through a lotus-based token exchange. To launch a Sybil attack, an attacker needs to control multiple vine-like agents. Each vine must exchange lotus tokens with genuine nodes, which incurs a non-negligible cost. This mechanism effectively deters Sybil attacks by ensuring that each artificial node must pay a price, making large-scalefake identities prohibitively expensive.
